section_summary: This section comprises U.S. Embassy monthly reports on conditions in Japan for July, August, September, and early October 1935, accompanied by a State Department Far Eastern Affairs summary memorandum. Major international questions documented include Japanese-American relations regarding the Petroleum Industry Law, proposed automotive manufacturing restrictions, Philippine textile export quotas, and the official visits to Japan of Secretary of War George H. Dern and Vice President John Nance Garner. Key regional and domestic developments include Japan's growing political and economic penetration of North China, the appointment of Yosuke Matsuoka as head of the South Manchuria Railway, the assassination of Major General Tetsuzan Nagata by Lieutenant Colonel Saburo Aizawa, the resignation of War Minister Senjuro Hayashi, and the intensifying government and military campaign against Dr. Tatsukichi Minobe's constitutional 'organ theory' of the Emperor.

subfiles.about: Concluding portion of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report on political, economic, military, and diplomatic conditions in Japan for July 1935, with schedules of despatches and telegrams sent.
subfiles.summary: Surveys the political controversy surrounding Dr. Minobe's institutional theory of the Emperor, inter-factional Army friction resulting in the replacement of Inspector General of Military Education General Jinsaburo Masaki by General Jotaro Watanabe, and inter-ministry negotiations over the 1936-37 national defense budget. Outlines developments in shipping consolidation (creation of Nanyo Kaiun), proposed protectionist legislation for the domestic automotive industry, civil aviation programs, and foreign trade statistics. Reports on a fatal earthquake in Taiwan and concludes with comprehensive summary lists of diplomatic despatches and telegrams sent to the Department of State during July 1935.
subfiles.title: Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of July, 1935 (Report No. 106, Enclosure to Despatch No. 1427)

subfiles.about: Summary memorandum by the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs reviewing highlights of the Tokyo Embassy's political report for August 1935.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Analyzes Japanese trade reactions to proposed Philippine legislative protection for American cotton cloth and the replacement of Count Hayashi by Yosuke Matsuoka as president of the South Manchuria Railway to spearhead economic penetration of North China. Reports on growing sentiment in Manchukuo favoring the withdrawal of extraterritorial privileges from non-recognizing powers and quotes Ambassador Tsuneo Matsudaira regarding British support for friendly relations with Japan. Notes proposed negotiations to revise the commercial treaty with French Indo-China, plans to open a Japanese legation in Addis Ababa, and preliminary ministry budget estimates for 1936-37.
subfiles.title: Tokyo's Political Report for August 1935

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting Report No. 107 on political, economic, military, and diplomatic developments in Japan during August 1935.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Details Japanese protests over a caricature of the Emperor in Vanity Fair and a disrespect incident in Seattle, foreign oil company resistance to storage requirements under the Petroleum Industry Law, draft legislation establishing a licensing system for the automobile industry, and informal Alaska salmon fishery discussions. Reviews North China border incidents, the appointment of Yosuke Matsuoka as South Manchuria Railway president, the formal decision to abolish Japanese extraterritoriality in Manchukuo, Ambassador Matsudaira's comments on British naval policy, and Japanese suspicion regarding Sir Frederick Leith-Ross's mission to China. Chronicles internal crises including the assassination of Military Affairs Bureau Director Major General Tetsuzan Nagata by Lieutenant Colonel Saburo Aizawa, the Okada Cabinet's formal statement condemning Dr. Minobe's organ theory, and concludes with lists of August despatches and telegrams.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1475: Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of August, 1935 (Report No. 107)

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting Report No. 108 surveying Japanese political, economic, military, and international affairs during September 1935.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports on the postponement to June 1936 of the six-month oil storage requirement under the Petroleum Industry Law, negotiations limiting Japanese cotton textile exports to the Philippines, and public anticipation of Vice President Garner's visit. Covers Major General Tada's aggressive public statements advocating North China separation from Nanking, the Tokyo consultations of British Economic Adviser Sir Frederick Leith-Ross, Egyptian tariff conflicts, and border frictions with Soviet Russia. Analyzes the resignation of War Minister Senjuro Hayashi following the Nagata assassination and his replacement by General Yoshiyuki Kawashima, Dr. Minobe's resignation from the House of Peers, Cabinet changes, and concludes with schedules of September despatches and telegrams.
subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of September, 1935 (Report No. 108)

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting the opening sections of Report No. 109, reporting on Japanese foreign relations and internal affairs during October 1935.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Documents the state visits to Japan of Secretary of War George H. Dern and Vice President John Nance Garner, accompanied by House Speaker Joseph W. Byrns and a 41-member congressional delegation en route to the inauguration of the Philippine Commonwealth. Discusses developments under the Petroleum Industry Law, including a sanctioned domestic gasoline price increase and foreign oil company reactions. Concludes mid-report with Cabinet approval of a new unified policy toward North China and the dispatch of Major General Neiji Okamura to China via Dairen to coordinate with Japanese military field commanders.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1542: Report on Conditions in Japan during the Month of October, 1935 (Report No. 109)
